textbookText: 8.2.6 PHYLUM ANNELIDA (L., ANNULUS-RING, EIDOS-FORM) The term annelida was coined by Lamarck for segmented worms which are regarded as first higher non- chordates.
1. They are mostly aquatic, found in both marine water and freshwater, some of them are terrestrial and burrowing form.

2. They are sedentary or free living and some of them are parasitic. 3. Body is elongated, vermiform, bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic. 4. There is organ system level of body organization. 5. They have metamerically segmented body in which external segmentation corresponds

internal segmentation. Segments are also called somites or metameres which are separated externally by grooves and internally by septa. 6. Their body wall consists of outermost non-living cuticle secreted by underlying epidermis and innermost layer of circular and longitudinal muscle fibres. 7. They have schizocoel i.e. true coelom which is divided by septa into coelomic chambers and leeches are haemocoelomate. 8. Locomotary organs are segmentally repeated chitinous bristles called setae or lateral fleshy outgrowth called parapodia or suckers in some forms. 9. Digestive system is straight tube like and complete. Digestion is extracellular. 10. There is closed type of blood vascular system. Blood is red because of haemoglobin or erythrocruorin dissolved in plasma. 11. Respiration takes place through general body surface or through gills of parapodia and head. 12. Excretory organs are segmentally arranged coiled tube-like structures called nephridia. 13. Nervous system consists of a nerve ring and double ventral nerve cord bearing ganglia and lateral nerves. 14. Sensory organs are touch receptor, taste buds, statocyst, photoreceptors and eyes. 15. They are mostly monoecious i.e. hermaphrodite. Some of them are unisexual too. 16. Asexual reproduction by regeneration is common and sexual reproduction takes place by the fusion of gametes. 17. Development is direct in hermaphrodite annelids. Indirect development is present in unisexual forms with a free-swimming larval form called trochophore larva.

Unique features Metamericlly segmented body, schizocoelomate and some haemocoelomate, locomotory organs are setae, parapodia and suckers, closed circulatory system, excrertion through nephridia, haemoglobin in plasma, Larva is trochophore if present.
